title: What Do Specialised Family Therapists Do Differently When Suspecting the Presence of Autism? A Qualitative Study
abstract: ABSTRACT Worldwide there is more and more awareness of the autism mental health crisis. There is a growing body of evidence supporting the use of family therapy for families where autism is present. Conversely, many family therapists may not feel competent when a family where autism is present seeks guidance. Until now, little has been known about what therapists who do feel competent do differently when meeting such families. This qualitative study uses constructivist grounded theory to explore the adaptations that family therapists make when counselling families where they suspect autism is present. Seven in‐depth interviews were conducted with specialised family therapists. These therapists described adaptations in their pace, style, contextualisation and setting. When done in this specific way, family therapy has the strong advantage of being able to bring problematic dynamics into the consultation room to search for the difference that makes the difference.
